unit.why: A single narrative: R. Barukh of Medzhybizh sends petitioners to a drunkard whose decree ends a plague, then tells them the drunkard's backstory of escaping a noblewoman's seduction after ransoming Jewish prisoners.

stories.start_quote: פ״א הי׳ צרה גדולה על ישראל
stories.summary_en: In a time of plague R. Barukh of Medzhybizh sends petitioners to a village drunkard. The drunkard's word stops the plague. The rebbe then reveals that the man was once a rich merchant who freed Jewish prisoners held by a noble widow and fled before sleeping with her, and so Heaven granted him the power that whatever he decrees comes to pass. Because his decrees could cancel heavenly judgments, the Attribute of Judgment made him a perpetual drunkard.
